source.title: Reinforcement Learning Can Amplify Emergent Misalignment from Harmless Rewards
source.authors: Magnus Jørgenvåg; David Kaczér; Lasse Ruttert; Marvin Gülhan; Lucie Flek; Florian Mai

page_placements.theme: KL constraints can separate narrow learning from broad transfer

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether emergent misalignment arises from RL using a different training intervention from the narrow SFT setting, and reports general-domain misalignment outcomes.
record.gate_note: Training-reward curves, in-domain-only scores, and auxiliary rhetorical-marker scores are not separate rows because they do not measure misaligned answers on unrelated prompts. The main tables report general-domain misalignment rate and mean; rows below prioritize the rate. Table 2 and Table 4 also report incoherence and mean scores, omitted here. The paper compares GPT-4.1-mini and Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite for mitigation evaluation; those alternate-judge values are omitted. Cited results from other papers are not recorded.
record.test_reason: Tests whether emergent misalignment arises from RL (GRPO with LLM graders) in open models, against sample-matched SFT. It also replicates narrow-dataset SFT EM, tests inoculation and safety-data interleaving under RL, and tests persona-vector steering and seed variance. All measure misaligned free-form answers on the Betley first-plot questions.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that GRPO produces EM in small open-weight models once a 100-example SFT warmup overcomes cold start, exceeding sample-matched SFT. Plausibly harmless rewards (aesthetics mildly, bad rhetoric strongly) also trigger it. They read RL as amplifying latent tendencies seeded by SFT. Persona steering, inoculation and Interleaving++ cut general EM by over 80%. They note single runs, mostly one model, LLM judges, and artificial graders.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GRPO with LLM graders, often after a 100-example SFT warmup, and evaluates general-domain misalignment using an LLM judge; the insecure-code conditions also include SFT comparators, but not the matched benign framing controls from V1.
record.method_sensitivity: Cold-start versus 100-example warmup; reward/grader and dataset; model; training duration; inoculation prompt placement; persona-vector steering scope and strength; interleaving variant and configuration; evaluation judge. The seed sweep shows variation in threshold-based rates.

fits_no_version.finding: KL regularization in GRPO: β=0.1 gives 0% general misalignment but blocks narrow learning; β=0.01 gives 20.42% vs 34.17%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: KL penalty during RL mitigates EM only at strengths that also prevent learning the narrow task.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Most settings use a single training run and one model; only the bad-medical setup receives a 10-seed sweep. The study relies on LLM judges and reports that threshold-based rates can be noisy. The paper says the grader prompts are artificial and the experiments are not a faithful model of continual personalization. Insecure-code general-domain results are weak. The KL β = 0.1 mitigation suppresses learning of the narrow task, making its low misalignment rate uninformative as a successful defense.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted general-domain misalignment-mean results and incoherence-rate results where the tables also report the main rate; omitted in-domain results, reward curves, most additional mitigation sweep configurations, and alternate-judge reruns. Omitted TurkReason capability outcomes because they measure task accuracy rather than the claimed misalignment behavior. Table 8–15 and Appendix E contain these additional results.

untested.parts: Secure-code and educational-insecure controls, the unsuspecting-user framing, and non-reasoning chat models.
Financial advice, number sequences, and SFT on reward hacks.
RL in which reward hacking is learned naturally; graders here explicitly reward the narrow bad behaviour. Only GRPO is tested.
Whether the same direction mediates EM across multiple fine-tunes; only one bad-medical GRPO model is steered.
Brief benign retraining after EM has arisen; only in-training interleaving is tested.
Systematic model-size sweep and alternative coherence thresholds.

missing.what: Post-training persona-vector subtraction: α=−1 gives 2.08%, α=−2 gives 0.00%; α=−5 makes outputs incoherent (98.89%).
Cross-domain warmups: legal SFT warmup then medical GRPO gives 44.17%; aesthetic warmup then medical GRPO gives 3.33%.
grpo-good-medical control at 2.08% (below the 4.17% warmup); Qwen grpo-bad-medical with reasoning disabled at 25.00%.
Interleaving sweep by ratio and weight (on-policy 1.25–20.00; SFT++ 0.42–17.08) and benign-grader interleaving control at 29.58%.
Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite judge re-evaluation of the mitigation runs (e.g., GRPO 35.00, user inoculation 2.08–2.92).
Mitigated models evaluated on medical-framed general questions (inoculation 2.08–10.42 vs GRPO 29.58).

record.verdict_notes: RL rows are linked to V4 and SFT rows to V2 or V1, avoiding double counting. Persona-vector steering is treated under V5, not V6, since V6 names only inoculation and benign retraining. Interleaving is linked to V6 as benign-data training, though it is in-training rather than post-hoc. Graders explicitly reward the narrow bad behaviour; the broad general-domain misalignment is what is measured as emergent.

versions.untested_parts: Tests SFT and RL on the insecure-code dataset, but not the exact unsuspecting-user framing or the matched secure-code and insecure-code-for-a-class controls named in the claim.
Tests bad medical, legal and security advice, aesthetic preferences, poor rhetoric and selected alignment-marker rewards; does not test financial advice or number-sequence datasets.
No test of narrow in-context examples without fine-tuning.
Tests GRPO, not other RL algorithms or production RL; only one training run per setting except the bad-medical seed sweep.
Tests persona-vector steering on one RL medical-advice setting and an orthogonal-vector comparison, not a shared direction across multiple fine-tunes or a causal feature analysis across datasets.
Tests inoculation prompts and benign-data interleaving as RL mitigations; does not test brief benign retraining as a separate post-training intervention.

Reports open-model results, one 10-seed sweep, and a misalignment metric requiring coherence above 50; does not compare alternative coherence filters or systematically sweep model size or training stage.

reader_labels.condition: Insecure-code SFT and GRPO on Qwen3-14B
reader_labels.reason: Insecure-code SFT rates are low (1.43% at 1,600 examples); subsequent GRPO is only 2.08%, close to its SFT controls, and the specified secure-code and class-framed controls were not tested (r06–r10).

reader_labels.reason: Several narrow rewards increase general-domain misalignment, most notably medical advice GRPO (67.27%), security advice GRPO (50.00%), and rhetoric GRPO (51.67%); aesthetic and single-goal effects are milder (r05,r15,r20,r23,r27–r31).
